passages.heading: HAUSE
passages.text:
A cinematic visual language for ideas, systems and explanations — not a component library, not brand guidelines. Extracted from [chrishayuk](https://github.com/chrishayuk/chrishayuk) once a second consumer (vindex3.org) made copy-pasting the design system across repos the wrong move.

Read `tokens.css` and the files under `components/` before this README — they're the source of truth. This file just explains how a project wires HAUSE in.

passages.heading: What's in here
passages.text:
```
tokens.css     palette, three type voices (editorial/system/evidence), 12-col grid,
               motion tokens, Light/Dark, status marks, reveal/pulse animations
types.ts       Status ("OPEN" | "ONGOING" | "SUPPORTED" | "REFUTED" | "SUPERSEDED")
components/
  Reveal.tsx          scroll-triggered reveal wrapper
  StatusMark.tsx       word + dot status indicator
  GridOverlay.tsx      "SHOW STRUCTURE" 12-column overlay
  PaceDemo.tsx         Immediate / Considered / Cinematic motion demo
  ModeToggle.tsx       LIGHT / DARK control
  Inquiry.tsx          "Ask the Codex"-style query -> real-form primitive
  forms/               the chapter primitives — all in one flat directory,
                        because the import path is the public API and it does
                        not move. The taxonomy below is documentation, not
                        directory structure.
```

passages.heading: The three modes
passages.text:
Every form under `forms/` is one of three kinds. The split was not designed
up front — it emerged from real chapters (the vindex3.org build), which is
the only way HAUSE accepts structure. The canonical index is
[`manifest.ts`](manifest.ts) — every consumer that counts or lists the
forms derives from it, so the lists below are prose, and the manifest is
the evidence.

**Statements** — prose forms in the three voices; server-renderable, no
interaction. The reader reads.
`Hero · Statement · Observation · Claim · Evidence · Question · Timeline ·
Connection · Refusal · Excerpt`

**Instruments** — interactive forms; understanding through manipulation.
The reader operates them, and every one carries a text fallback so the
point survives with the interaction removed.
`Anatomy · Decomposition · ExpertField · Comparison · Variants · Ladder ·
Agreement · Derivation · ByteMap · FollowReveal · Terminal · Gating ·
Provenance · Citation`

(`Inquiry` lives outside `forms/` — a routing primitive over the real
forms, not a form itself.)

**Performances** — cinematic forms; they play themselves. In-view start, a
designed resting state (which is what reduced-motion and no-JS get), REPLAY
where the piece runs once, a gentle in-view loop where a scrolling reader
must never find it finished. Never a crossfade between two physical forms
of one thing — staged swaps only.
`Film · Transformation · Unfol

passages.heading: Sound — the tactile voice
passages.text:
`sound.ts` is a synthesized palette (sine waves and envelopes, no audio
files): `tick` for a selection, `swap` for a staged swap committing,
`settle` for a performance finishing, `refuse` for a fail-closed moment.
Opt-in via `SoundToggle` (localStorage `hause-sound`), off by default —
hause sound is chosen, never inflicted. Loops stay silent; only
interactions and completions speak. Peak gains sit far below speech
level: a well-made drawer closing, not an app chirping.

**HAUSE knows nothing about any specific site's content model.** No file here imports from outside this package. `Inquiry` takes a `resolve` function as a prop rather than importing one — the caller (the site) supplies what a query means; HAUSE only supplies how the result is experienced. That boundary is the whole point of this being a separate repo.

passages.heading: Using it in a project
Light / Dark
passages.text:
Two authored environments, not a `prefers-color-scheme` inversion — default light, explicit opt-in via `ModeToggle`, `data-mode="dark"` on `<html>` flips the `--bg`/`--fg` tokens. To avoid a flash on load, each consuming site's `layout.tsx` needs a small blocking inline script in `<head>` that reads `localStorage` before paint, plus `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` for the resulting (expected) attribute mismatch. Copy this verbatim rather than reinventing it — see any consuming site's `layout.tsx`:

```html
<script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html:
  `try{var m=localStorage.getItem('hause-mode');if(m==='dark')document.documentElement.dataset.mode='dark';}catch(e){}`
}} />
```

passages.heading: Design principles (the ones that matter for extension)
passages.text:
- **No generic card kit.** Every `forms/*` component is a specific, semantic thing — a Statement is not a styled div, it's an editorial-voice claim with its own scale and rhythm. If you're about to add a `Card` component, stop.
- **A Mode gets built for a real chapter, not manufactured as a demo.** `ExpertField` (Simulation) and `Comparison` (one object, two interpretations) both exist because a real exhibition needed them, in that order, discovered through making — not designed as an abstract taxonomy up front. When adding a new Mode, build it against real content first.
- **Always-present text fallback.** Every interactive form (`Decomposition`, `ExpertField`, `Comparison`) renders a plain-language sentence describing its point even with the interaction removed — for `prefers-reduced-motion`, no-JS, and crawlers. Keep this pattern.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion` gets a designed static state, not just `animation: none`.** Check `Reveal`, `.graph-pulse`, `.pace-demo-box` in `tokens.css` for the pattern.

passages.heading: Machine legibility — SEO and AEO as design-system concerns
passages.text:
HAUSE is a design system for AI, and that cuts both ways: AIs compose
answers *from* the forms, and machines — crawlers, answer engines, agent
browsers — must be able to *read* what the forms say. Legibility to
machines is not an afterthought bolted onto a site; it is part of the
grammar, carried by the library itself:

- **The `Answer` form.** A natural-language question as a real heading and
  a 40–100 word answer a reader or a machine can lift whole, with a stable
  anchor so the exact question is citable — not just the page. It sits
  beneath the editorial surface and says the plain thing plainly; the
  beautiful heading keeps its job.
- **`seo.ts` + `JsonLd`.** Builders that emit structured data from records
  a site already holds — WebSite, TechArticle, BreadcrumbList, DefinedTerm
  (a knowledge-graph entity, said in schema.org), SoftwareApplication,
  QAPage. The crawlable answer can never drift from the rendered one,
  because both project from the same record.
- **Query-shaped `<title>`, designed headings.** The browser title says
  what the page answers, in the words people search with; the visible
  HAUSE heading stays exactly as designed. You get both, always.
- **ARIA state on every instrument.** Agent browsers read `aria-pressed`,
  `aria-expanded`, and labels to understand interactive interfaces — the
  Terminal's DESIGNED|RAW|GRAPH tabs carry them, and every new

passages.heading: Provenance and citation — publishing as a design-system concern
passages.text:
A design system for AI has to model the objects an AI actually reasons
over. Buttons and cards are not those objects; claims, evidence,
sources and provenance are. Citation is where that stops being a thesis
and becomes machinery, so HAUSE carries it: `cite.ts`, and two forms.

**One record, four surfaces.** A `CitationRecord` — title, authors,
first-publication date, version, canonical URL, and whatever
identifiers actually exist — projects onto all four places a
publication has to exist at once, and can never drift between them:

- **the page** — `Provenance`, one quiet line (published · revised ·
  version · DOI where there is one) that expands to the full record:
  the commit, the artifact hash, the archive record, the dated history
  of how the work came to be said.
- **the export** — `Citation`, the reference in the formats people
  paste. Three, not six: BibTeX for LaTeX, APA for prose, CSL-JSON
  because every reference manager turns it into the other three hundred.
- **the head** — `citationMeta()` emits `citation_*` tags, which is how
  Zotero, Scholar and every "add to library" button read a page without
  being told anything about your site. Spread it into Next's
  `metadata.other`.
- **the graph** — `citationLd()` in `seo.ts`, the same record said in
  schema.org, with identifiers as PropertyValues.

**Two levels, one system.** Everything substantive is *citable by

passages.heading: Hero — statement
passages.text: Hero is a statement. The room's first wall: kicker, headline, dek.

passages.heading: Statement — statement
passages.text: Statement is a statement. One sentence, given the whole width.

passages.heading: Observation — statement
passages.text: Observation is a statement. A labelled paragraph that watches rather than argues.

passages.heading: Claim — statement
passages.text: Claim is a statement. An assertion that knows it must answer to evidence.

passages.heading: Evidence — statement
passages.text: Evidence is a statement. Rows of labelled findings with status marks — receipts, not decoration.

passages.heading: Question — statement
passages.text: Question is a statement. An open question given the same typographic dignity as an answer.

passages.heading: Timeline — statement
passages.text: Timeline is a statement. Dated entries, in order — history as prose, not a widget.

passages.heading: Connection — statement
passages.text: Connection is a statement. A bridge out of the chapter: one sentence, then the doors.

passages.heading: Refusal — statement
passages.text: Refusal is a statement. Fail-closed rendered as design language, not as an error state. Originated in vindex3.

passages.heading: Excerpt — statement
passages.text: Excerpt is a statement. Someone else's words, typeset — verbatim source material with its markdown rendered and its trims marked. Originated in vindex3 · Ask (2026-08-29).

passages.heading: Answer — statement
passages.text: Answer is a statement. The question asked the way people ask it, answered first — one lift-able paragraph beneath the editorial surface, addressable by anchor. Originated in vindex3 · the legibility layer (2026-08-30).

passages.heading: Snippet — statement
passages.text: Snippet is a statement. A labeled block of code or terminal output, verbatim on the ink — the on-ramp form, promoted when two sites needed the same shape. Originated in hause.design · Use (2026-08-30).

passages.heading: Anatomy — instrument
passages.text: Anatomy is a instrument. An annotated cutaway — one artifact drawn as its layers, fully disclosed.

passages.heading: Decomposition — instrument
passages.text: Decomposition is a instrument. One object, its parts, the thing that assembles them — stepped by hand.

passages.heading: ExpertField — instrument
passages.text: ExpertField is a instrument. A field of units, mostly dormant; each scenario lights the subset that answers. Originated in the codex.

passages.heading: Comparison — instrument
passages.text: Comparison is a instrument. One object, two interpretations, dragged between. Originated in the codex.

passages.heading: Variants — instrument
passages.text: Variants is a instrument. Physically present variants of one identity — and a designed refusal for the absent one. Originated in vindex3.

passages.heading: Ladder — instrument
passages.text: Ladder is a instrument. A gated progression — rungs climbed in order, each closed only by its own criterion. Originated in vindex3.

passages.heading: Agreement — instrument
passages.text: Agreement is a instrument. N independently-derived values that must be identical — with a FAIL row.

passages.heading: Derivation — instrument
passages.text: Derivation is a instrument. A value folded down a graded scale by caps — derived, never asserted.

passages.heading: ByteMap — instrument
passages.text: ByteMap is a instrument. A physical layout drawn to scale — each field's width is its width in bytes.

passages.heading: FollowReveal — instrument
passages.text: FollowReveal is a instrument. A path through connected ideas, replayed at the hause stagger.

passages.heading: Terminal — instrument
passages.text: Terminal is a instrument. A query surface whose chrome is the form and whose meaning is one executor. Originated in vindex3 · the Explorer (2026-08-29).

passages.heading: Gating — instrument
passages.text: Gating is a instrument. A stream widened into a working space, judged channel by channel, brought back home. Originated in vindex3 · the Anatomy (2026-08-29).

passages.heading: Provenance — instrument
passages.text: Provenance is a instrument. The publication record beneath the page — dates, version, identifiers, history — disclosed on demand, absent where nothing is registered. Originated in vindex3 · citing the specification (2026-08-31).

passages.heading: Citation — instrument
passages.text: Citation is a instrument. The reference itself, in the formats people paste — plain, BibTeX, APA, CSL-JSON, all from one record. Originated in vindex3 · citing the specification (2026-08-31).

passages.heading: Transformation — performance
passages.text: Transformation is a performance. Comparison's cinematic sibling — identical props, performed. Originated in vindex3.

passages.heading: Unfolding — performance
passages.text: Unfolding is a performance. Decomposition's cinematic sibling — the parts arrive on their own. Originated in vindex3.

passages.heading: Compilation — performance
passages.text: Compilation is a performance. A pile of inputs compiled down through named stages. Originated in vindex3.

passages.heading: Procession — performance
passages.text: Procession is a performance. One thing passing through every stage, in order. Originated in vindex3.

passages.heading: Magnitude — performance
passages.text: Magnitude is a performance. A powers-of-ten zoom-out — each arrival rescales the world. Originated in vindex3.

passages.heading: Channel — performance
passages.text: Channel is a performance. Throughput through a fixed-capacity conduit. Originated in vindex3.

passages.heading: Quantisation — performance
passages.text: Quantisation is a performance. What quantisation actually does, performed on a lattice. Originated in vindex3.

passages.heading: Film — performance
passages.text: Film is a performance. A short film in the flow of a chapter — poster until it earns the play. Originated in vindex3. Held, not yet exhibited.
